newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zairean rebels say enter city of Kisangani.
newsitem.headline: Zairean rebels say enter city of Kisangani.

text.p: A senior Zairean rebel commander said on Monday that rebels had entered Kisangani, the largest city in eastern Zaire, and were in control of parts of it.

Commander John Kabunga, senior aide to rebel leader Laurent Kabila, told Reuters in the town of Goma that rebel forces had reached Kisangani from the east by bypassing the intervening town of Walikale, where they had encountered difficulties.
"Parts of our forces are now in control of parts of Kisangani. We went there by bypassing the town of Walikale, which is still giving us problems," Kabunga said.
Kabunga said rebel forces had also tried to enter the town of Bunia beyond Beni, which is in rebel hands, but had encountered resistance from the heavily fortified town.
"There are a lot of Zairean soldiers in Bunia. At the moment things are hard for us there," Kabunga added.

Kabila earlier told reporters in Bukavu that his forces had captured the gold and diamong mining centre of Kamituga on the southern front and Beni on the northern front. He said the foreign staff at Kamituga, where South Africa's Anglo-American corporation has substantial interests, had fled westwards.
